newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - MARKKA SEEN VOLATILE, STOCKS TO TRACK U.S..
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - MARKKA SEEN VOLATILE, STOCKS TO TRACK U.S..

text.p: Outlook for Finnish financial markets next week according to analysts:
*Finnish markka seen remaining volatile amid ongoing speculation, could strengthen if domestic November GDP data due on Thursday show stronger-than-expected growth,
*Finnish bonds to track German bunds,
*Good demand seen for 2001 bond in Thursday's auction,
*U.S. economic data key for stock market sentiment. MARKKA SEEN VOLATILE, STRONG GDP GROWTH MAY HELP IT FIRM
The fate of the markka will be in the hands of overseas speculators next week -- with high volatility expected to continue in the Finnish unit, domestic operators said.
"The key question is what overseas investors will do next week," one analyst said.
If November GDP showed stronger-than-forecast growth the markka could firm against the mark, Postipankki economist Kirsi Hirvonen said.
Postipankki forecast November GDP growth at around four percent year-on-year. Danish Unibank's forecast is six percent.
In October, GDP rose by 5.7 percent year-on-year. November GDP data will be released on Thursday at 0700/0500 GMT.
Bond market investors will continue to look to German Bunds for direction, analysts said. No large swings are expected on the market. GOOD DEMAND SEEN IN AUCTION OF 2001 BENCHMARK
The State Treasury Office (STO) will auction two government bonds on Thursday: the 2001 benchmark, and the 2010 bond.
Lively demand was seen particularly for the 2001 paper.
Analysts said the long-end of the yield curve has recently become more attractive due to abundant liquidity.

Part of the liqudity will be channeled into T-bills with operators expecting auction volumes to remain at recent high levels. STO will hold its regular T-bill auction on Tuesday with results due after 1330/1130 GMT.
The following T-bill maturities to be auctioned: 105-days, 228-days and 350-days. U.S. ECONOMIC DATA KEY FOR FINNISH STOCKS
The stock market will keep monitoring Wall Street for direction, analysts said.
U.S. Q4 employment costs are due at 1530/1330 GMT on Tuesday and U.S. Q4 GDP will be released on Friday at 1530/1330 GMT.
These indicators will give clues about the direction of the U.S. economy.
"If (Q4 employment costs) turn out to be stronger than forecast it will shake the markets," said Risto Murto, head of research at Selin Finance, adding stock would fall. BENEFON PROFIT SEEN HALVING
Santasalo-JOT will release its 1996 earnings next Monday at 1400/1200 GMT, Kesla will report 1996 earnings and Talentum preliminary 1996 earnings on Thursday.

Benefon's 1996 report is due on Friday. Eight analysts's median forecast for Benefon's full-year 1996 profit before extraordinary items and tax was 33 million markka, down from last year's 74 million.
These results are not expected to have any impact on market sentiment, analysts said.
--Tuula Franck, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 240
